idee_recherchee.texte: Quantum entanglement links particles so that measuring one instantly affects the other no matter the distance, and some theorists believe that entanglement is the thread from which spacetime itself is woven.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Analogie de la chaleur : l'espace-temps comme phénomène émergent
resume: Heat in hot water feels real, yet a single molecule only has kinetic energy, so heat emerges from many colliding molecules. Theoretical physicists apply the same logic to space-time, saying it is a byproduct emerging from a vast network of entangled quantum particles exchanging information.
texte: If you pour boiling water into a cup and you touch it, it feels hot. You'll notice a rise in temperature. But if you zoom in and you look at an individual molecule of water, it does not have an increase in temperature. It just has an increase in kinetic energy. It is moving fast. The heat you feel is a byproduct of large amounts of energy across large amounts of molecules, all interacting and colliding with one another. It's real to us because we can feel it in our fingertips. But on a subatomic level, it's not real. And today's theoretical physicists are taking that logic and applying it to space and time. Space-time, they say, is not a stage or a fabric. It's closer to a byproduct. Just as heat emerges from the chaotic motion of molecules, physical space and time emerges from the unimaginably vast network of entangled quantum particles constantly swapping information.
